objective: Add a pure in-process Cloud IaC OpenTofu module-registry route boundary that maps official GET discovery, versions, and download paths into the existing API DTO boundary while preserving no REST server, live endpoint, auth runtime, database/object-store, signing, SLSA/VSA, tofu plan/apply, provider runtime, FD-001 dogfood tenant workload hosting, or cloud provisioning claims.

best_practice_sources.what_it_establishes: OpenTofu discovery begins with GET /.well-known/terraform.json and identifies modules.v1 service bases.
OpenTofu module registry v1 versions and download operations are GET routes relative to the modules.v1 base URL.
Module registry sources are the native versioned distribution mechanism for reusable modules; private registries need credentials and should not embed secrets in module source definitions.

implemented_claims: Added CloudIacModuleRegistryRouteRequest and CloudIacModuleRegistryRouteResponse as pure in-process route-boundary DTOs with data_class comments.
Added route_module_registry_request to dispatch official OpenTofu discovery, versions, and download GET paths into the existing API DTO boundary.
Added MethodNotAllowed and RouteNotFound errors for wrong method and unknown/incomplete route rejection before any runtime adapter exists.

Tests prove official route dispatch, non-GET rejection, exact method/path matching, incomplete-path rejection, and route-specific authorization surface checks without adding dependencies or HTTP runtime.
Updated Cloud IaC manifest/tasks/evidence/audit with route-boundary scope and explicit FD-001 dogfood non-claim.
Hardened route matching to reject whitespace-mutated methods and paths instead of trimming before dispatch.
explicit_non_claims: no REST server or HTTP listener/router runtime
no registry publish path or object-store serving
no authentication or Cedar runtime integration beyond in-process authorization metadata checks
no module signing or Sigstore/cosign execution
no SLSA or VSA attestation generation
no provider runtime, provider API calls, provider credentials, or cloud provisioning
no FD-001 microservice dogfood tenant workload hosting or production tenant workload evidence
false_green_findings_closed: Avoided claiming an HTTP service: the new code is an in-process route boundary only.
Avoided treating OpenTofu protocol fixtures as live endpoint evidence.
Avoided treating route dispatch tests as auth runtime, persistence, module signing, or provider execution evidence.
Preserved FD-001 dogfood tenant workload hosting as a future substrate proof rather than a current claim.
known_gaps: Full ./bin/oya verify --ci-required is not claimed by this ChangeSet; repo-wide unrelated blockers remain outside this Cloud IaC slice.

Cloud IaC still needs future slices for an actual REST/HTTP registry server, live service discovery and module versions/download endpoints, registry publish path, object-store serving, authentication/Cedar runtime integration, database adapter, module signing/Sigstore/cosign, SLSA attestations, independent provider provenance/VSA verification, tofu tests, plan/apply evidence, provider-resource-complete modules, and live GitOps/provider integration evidence.

FD-001 remains the master-plan product delivery goal and Oyatie Cloud must later prove itself by hosting FD-001 microservices as tenant workloads; this ChangeSet provides no tenant-workload dogfood evidence.
Concurrent unrelated application-shell and other agent work exists in the worktree; this ChangeSet does not claim or modify those surfaces.

findings: Adds the smallest route-dispatch layer in the existing API crate, avoiding a premature server or abstraction stack.
Locks protocol route semantics needed for future module registry service bootstrap while retaining operational non-claims until runtime evidence exists.
FD-001 dogfood tenant workload hosting remains a future substrate proof, not a claim in this ChangeSet.
Wrong methods, incomplete paths, and missing route-specific authorization surfaces are rejected in tests.
Whitespace-mutated methods and paths are rejected by exact-match tests.
Route request/response types are simple Rust DTOs suitable for a future HTTP adapter.
No new dependencies; fmt, tests, check, clippy, and gate regressions passed.
Chose in-process route boundary over REST server to avoid false endpoint readiness while still advancing shared contract lock.
Authorization identifiers/surfaces are checked before route-specific DTO construction; no secrets or credentials are introduced.
Route matching is exact; inputs are not trimmed into valid OpenTofu routes.
Route parsing is bounded by a few path segments and allocates only small DTO strings.
Evidence and audit chain record local-only scope and non-claims.
Routes mirror OpenTofu remote service discovery and module registry v1 docs for discovery, versions, and download.
Manifest, tasks/plan, tasks/todo, evidence, and audit chain updated with route-boundary scope.
Future runtime adapters can dispatch into this boundary; no runtime operation is claimed now.
Oya VCS claim/work lifecycle used; no raw git/gh; sanctioned primitive policy preserved.
OpenTofu official docs used for route shapes; repo-local manifest/tasks distinguish evidence from future work.
Explicitly excludes live endpoints, auth runtime, persistence, signing/SLSA, provider runtime, plan/apply, cloud provisioning, full verify, and FD-001 tenant workload hosting.
